An apparatus for delivering a bolus of a medical agent to a patient is provided. The apparatus comprises a pump mechanism, a data input device, and a processor in data communication with the keypad and configured to control the pump mechanism. The processor is programmed to receive, through the data port, data specifying a bolus amount, data specifying a duration, and a percentage. The percentage defines a portion of the bolus amount to be delivered immediately upon execution of a delivery command, with the remainder of the bolus amount to be delivered over the specified duration. The processor is further programmed to execute the delivery command, thereby controlling the pump mechanism to deliver the bolus.

Also provided is a method for temporarily adjusting the delivery rate of an infusion pump programmed to deliver at a basal rate. The method comprises prompting a user to select whether to enter the temporary rate as a percentage of the current delivery rate or as a new delivery rate; entering into the pump a period of time having a beginning and an end; entering a temporary basal rate into the pump; and delivering the therapeutic agent at a delivery rate substantially equal to the temporary basal rate during the specified period.
outputs.L2:
A device is provided for administering a bolus of a medical agent to a patient. The device includes a pumping mechanism, a data-entry unit, and a processor that communicates with the keypad and controls operation of the pumping mechanism. The processor is configured to obtain, through the data port, information identifying the bolus quantity, the delivery duration, and a percentage. That percentage specifies the fraction of the bolus to be administered immediately when a delivery command is initiated, while the remaining fraction is delivered over the specified duration. Upon execution of the delivery command, the processor operates the pumping mechanism to administer the bolus.

A method is also provided for temporarily modifying the delivery rate of an infusion pump programmed to operate at a basal rate. The method includes asking the user to choose whether the temporary rate will be entered as a percentage of the existing delivery rate or as a replacement delivery rate. A time interval with a defined start and end is entered into the pump, along with a temporary basal rate. During that interval, the pump delivers the therapeutic agent at a rate substantially equal to the entered temporary basal rate.
outputs.L3:
The apparatus delivers a bolus of a medical agent through a pump mechanism controlled by a processor. The processor receives data specifying the total bolus amount, the duration of delivery, and the percentage of the bolus to be administered immediately. Upon receiving a delivery command, the processor directs the pump to administer the specified percentage at once. The pump then delivers the remainder of the bolus over the selected duration.

The infusion pump can also temporarily modify its programmed basal delivery rate for a defined period. Users may enter the temporary rate either as a percentage of the current basal rate or as a new delivery rate. At the end of the defined period, the pump may resume its previously programmed basal delivery rate.
outputs.L4:
The apparatus and method provide controlled administration of a therapeutic agent through an infusion pump. A user interface receives inputs defining a bolus, including the total bolus amount, the duration over which at least part of the bolus is to be delivered, and the percentage of the bolus designated for immediate delivery. A controller uses these inputs to divide the total bolus into an immediate portion and an extended portion. The immediate portion is delivered substantially at the start of the bolus operation, while the remaining portion is delivered over the specified duration at a calculated rate. The system may display the resulting amounts, rates, and delivery schedule for user review before initiating infusion.

The apparatus also supports temporary modification of an ongoing basal delivery program. A user may specify the temporary basal rate either as a percentage of the currently programmed basal rate or as a new absolute delivery rate. The user also enters the period for which the temporary rate is to remain active. In response, the controller calculates or applies the requested temporary rate, operates the pump at that rate for the defined period, and then returns the pump to its previously programmed basal schedule unless the temporary setting is canceled or otherwise changed.

By combining immediate and time-distributed bolus delivery with temporary basal-rate control, the system accommodates changing therapeutic requirements without requiring permanent modification of the underlying basal program. The approach allows delivery parameters to be entered in forms convenient to the user while enabling the pump to calculate and execute the corresponding infusion profile. Validation, confirmation, status-display, alarm, cancellation, and delivery-recording functions may also be incorporated to promote accurate and traceable administration. Thus, the apparatus and method provide flexible and precise control over the timing and rate at which insulin or another therapeutic agent is delivered.

**The Power of Simple Words**

The word **“the”** is one of the most common words in English. It points to a specific person, place, object, or idea, helping readers understand exactly what is being discussed. **“Also”** connects information by adding another thought or detail. Together, these simple words make sentences clearer and ideas easier to follow. Although they may seem ordinary, they are essential tools in everyday communication.

counterfactuals.output: An infusion pump system includes a fluid delivery mechanism, a user interface, and a controller configured to administer a bolus in multiple delivery phases. In response to receiving a bolus amount and a delivery-duration setting, the controller causes a first portion of the bolus to be delivered substantially immediately and a remaining portion to be delivered over the specified duration according to a selected delivery profile. The controller is further configured to implement a temporary basal-rate adjustment by increasing, decreasing, or suspending a programmed basal infusion rate for a defined time interval, after which the programmed basal infusion rate is automatically restored. The controller may coordinate bolus delivery with the temporary basal-rate adjustment, monitor cumulative delivery, and limit or modify delivery based on stored safety parameters, fluid-delivery status, or user confirmation. The system may display the immediate portion, extended portion, delivery duration, temporary basal rate, and corresponding completion times and may generate alerts in response to interrupted, incomplete, or out-of-range delivery.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write claims describing a medical infusion apparatus with a pump, keypad, and processor configured for dual-wave bolus delivery, plus a method for temporarily changing the pump’s basal delivery rate.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **A medical infusion apparatus comprising:**  
   a reservoir configured to contain a liquid medicament;  
   a pump mechanism operatively coupled to the reservoir and configured to deliver the liquid medicament to a patient;  
   a keypad configured to receive user input; and  
   a processor operatively coupled to the pump mechanism and the keypad, the processor configured to:  
   receive, through the keypad, programming information defining a bolus dose, an immediate-delivery portion of the bolus dose, and an extended-delivery interval;  
   control the pump mechanism to deliver the immediate-delivery portion over a first time period; and  
   control the pump mechanism to deliver a remaining portion of the bolus dose over the extended-delivery interval, thereby providing dual-wave bolus delivery.

2. The medical infusion apparatus of claim 1, wherein the immediate-delivery portion is specified as a percentage or an amount of the bolus dose.

3. The medical infusion apparatus of claim 1, wherein the processor is configured to cause delivery of the immediate-delivery portion before delivery of the remaining portion begins.

4. The medical infusion apparatus of claim 1, wherein the processor is configured to cause delivery of at least part of the immediate-delivery portion concurrently with delivery of the remaining portion.

5. The medical infusion apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a display, wherein the processor is configured to present, on the display, a prompt for at least one of the bolus dose, the immediate-delivery portion, or the extended-delivery interval.

6. The medical infusion apparatus of claim 1, wherein the processor is further configured to deliver the liquid medicament at a programmed basal delivery rate while controlling delivery of the remaining portion.

7. The medical infusion apparatus of claim 6, wherein the processor is configured to suspend, reduce, or continue basal delivery during delivery of the immediate-delivery portion.

8. The medical infusion apparatus of claim 1, wherein the processor is configured to calculate a delivery rate for the remaining portion based on the remaining portion and the extended-delivery interval.

9. The medical infusion apparatus of claim 1, wherein the processor is configured to receive a command, during delivery of the remaining portion, to cancel or modify the dual-wave bolus delivery.

10. The medical infusion apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a memory storing one or more basal-rate schedules and instructions executable by the processor to control the pump mechanism according to a selected basal-rate schedule.

11. **A method of temporarily changing a basal delivery rate of a medical infusion pump, the method comprising:**  
    operating the medical infusion pump according to a programmed basal delivery rate;  
    receiving, through a keypad of the medical infusion pump, a temporary-basal input specifying a temporary basal delivery parameter and a temporary duration;  
    determining, by a processor of the medical infusion pump, a temporary basal delivery rate based on the temporary basal delivery parameter;  
    controlling, by the processor, a pump mechanism to deliver a liquid medicament at the temporary basal delivery rate during the temporary duration; and  
    in response to expiration of the temporary duration, automatically controlling the pump mechanism to resume delivery according to the programmed basal delivery rate.

12. The method of claim 11, wherein the temporary basal delivery parameter comprises a percentage of the programmed basal delivery rate.

13. The method of claim 11, wherein the temporary basal delivery parameter comprises an absolute delivery rate.

14. The method of claim 11, further comprising receiving, before expiration of the temporary duration, a cancellation input and, in response, resuming delivery according to the programmed basal delivery rate.

15. The method of claim 11, further comprising limiting the temporary basal delivery rate or the temporary duration according to a stored safety limit.

16. The method of claim 11, wherein the programmed basal delivery rate varies according to a time-based basal schedule, and wherein automatically resuming delivery comprises identifying a basal rate specified by the time-based basal schedule for a time at which the temporary duration expires.

17. The method of claim 11, further comprising displaying an indication of the temporary basal delivery rate and a remaining portion of the temporary duration.

18. The method of claim 11, further comprising generating an alert before or upon expiration of the temporary duration.

19. The method of claim 11, wherein controlling the pump mechanism at the temporary basal delivery rate occurs concurrently with delivery of an extended portion of a dual-wave bolus.

20. **A medical infusion apparatus comprising:**  
    a pump mechanism configured to deliver a liquid medicament;  
    a keypad configured to receive a temporary-basal input;  
    a memory configured to store a basal delivery schedule; and  
    a processor configured to:  
    control the pump mechanism according to the basal delivery schedule;  
    determine, from the temporary-basal input, a temporary basal delivery rate and a temporary duration;  
    control the pump mechanism according to the temporary basal delivery rate during the temporary duration; and  
    automatically return control of the pump mechanism to the basal delivery schedule upon expiration or cancellation of the temporary duration.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate formal patent language for a programmable therapeutic-agent pump featuring split bolus administration and time-limited basal-rate modification.
counterfactuals.output:
## Exemplary Patent Specification Language

### Title

**Programmable Therapeutic-Agent Pump with Split Bolus Delivery and Time-Limited Basal-Rate Modification**

### Abstract

A programmable infusion system is configured to deliver a therapeutic agent according to a basal delivery schedule and to administer a requested bolus as a plurality of temporally separated bolus portions. A controller receives a bolus request, determines respective quantities and delivery times for the bolus portions, and controls a drive mechanism to deliver the bolus portions in accordance with a split-bolus profile. The controller is further configured to implement a temporary basal-rate modification having a defined duration, upon expiration of which the system automatically resumes a scheduled basal rate. In certain embodiments, the controller coordinates the split-bolus profile and the temporary basal-rate modification while enforcing one or more delivery limits based on therapeutic-agent delivery history, monitored physiological data, reservoir status, fault conditions, or combinations thereof.

---

## Technical Field

The present disclosure relates generally to ambulatory and implantable infusion devices and, more particularly, to programmable pumps that deliver a therapeutic agent according to basal and bolus delivery parameters.

---

## Summary

In one aspect, a therapeutic-agent delivery system includes a reservoir, a delivery mechanism fluidly coupled to the reservoir, a controller operatively coupled to the delivery mechanism, and a memory storing a basal delivery schedule. The controller is configured to receive a request for a bolus quantity and divide the bolus quantity into at least a first bolus portion and a second bolus portion. The first bolus portion is delivered during a first delivery interval, and the second bolus portion is delivered during a later delivery interval separated from the first delivery interval by a programmed delay or an extended-delivery period.

The controller is additionally configured to receive a temporary basal-rate command defining at least one modified basal rate and a finite modification duration. During the modification duration, the controller controls delivery according to the modified basal rate. Upon expiration, cancellation, or termination of the modification duration, the controller automatically restores a basal rate specified by the basal delivery schedule without requiring a further user command.

In some implementations, the controller coordinates basal and bolus delivery by suspending, offsetting, interleaving, or concurrently accounting for basal delivery during administration of one or more bolus portions. Delivery may be constrained by a maximum single-delivery quantity, a maximum delivery rate, a cumulative dose limit, an active-agent estimate, or a physiological-safety threshold.

---

## Exemplary Claims

### 1. Independent System Claim

1. **A programmable therapeutic-agent delivery system, comprising:**

   a reservoir configured to contain a therapeutic agent;

   a delivery mechanism fluidly coupled to the reservoir and configured to deliver the therapeutic agent to a patient;

   a memory storing a basal delivery schedule; and

   a controller operatively coupled to the delivery mechanism and the memory, the controller being configured to:

   receive a bolus command specifying a requested bolus quantity;

   generate, from the requested bolus quantity, a split-bolus profile comprising at least a first bolus portion and a second bolus portion, the second bolus portion being scheduled for delivery after commencement of delivery of the first bolus portion;

   operate the delivery mechanism to deliver the first bolus portion and the second bolus portion in accordance with the split-bolus profile;

   receive a temporary basal command specifying a modified basal rate and a finite modification duration;

   operate the delivery mechanism according to the modified basal rate during the finite modification duration; and

   automatically resume, upon termination of the finite modification duration, delivery according to a basal rate determined from the basal delivery schedule.

### 2. Dependent Claims

2. The system of claim 1, wherein the split-bolus profile specifies the first bolus portion as a percentage or quantity of the requested bolus quantity and specifies the second bolus portion as a remainder of the requested bolus quantity.

3. The system of claim 1, wherein the second bolus portion is delivered continuously over an extended-delivery interval.

4. The system of claim 1, wherein the split-bolus profile comprises three or more bolus portions having respective delivery times.

5. The system of claim 1, wherein the finite modification duration is defined by at least one of a start time, an end time, an elapsed duration, a monitored physiological condition, or completion of a programmed therapeutic event.

6. The system of claim 1, wherein the modified basal rate comprises an absolute delivery rate, an increment or decrement relative to the basal delivery schedule, or a percentage of a scheduled basal rate.

7. The system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to determine the basal rate to be resumed based on a time-dependent segment of the basal delivery schedule that is active when the finite modification duration terminates.

8. The system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to terminate the modified basal rate in response to at least one of expiration of the finite modification duration, receipt of a cancellation command, detection of a fault condition, detection of a reservoir condition, or satisfaction of a physiological threshold.

9. The system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to modify, postpone, reduce, suspend, or cancel the second bolus portion in response to physiological data received after delivery of the first bolus portion.

10. The system of claim 9, further comprising a physiological sensor or a communication interface configured to receive the physiological data from an external sensor.

11. The system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to calculate an active-agent quantity based on a delivery history and to constrain at least one of the split-bolus profile or the modified basal rate according to the active-agent quantity.

12. The system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to account for basal delivery occurring during delivery of the second bolus portion such that a cumulative quantity delivered during a selected interval does not exceed a programmed delivery limit.

13. The system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to interrupt the modified basal rate during delivery of at least one bolus portion and to resume the modified basal rate for a remaining portion of the finite modification duration.

14. The system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to preserve an originally programmed end time of the finite modification duration when the modified basal rate is interrupted.

15. The system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to extend the finite modification duration by an interruption interval during which the modified basal rate is not delivered.

16. The system of claim 1, further comprising a user interface configured to present, before delivery, an indication of the respective quantities and timing of the first and second bolus portions and an indication of the modified basal rate and the finite modification duration.

17. The system of claim 1, wherein the therapeutic agent comprises insulin, glucagon, an analgesic, a chemotherapeutic agent, an antibiotic, a hormone, or a biologic agent.

18. The system of claim 1, wherein the delivery mechanism comprises a motor-driven plunger, a peristaltic mechanism, a piston mechanism, an electroosmotic mechanism, or a positive-displacement micropump.

---

### 19. Independent Method Claim

19. **A computer-implemented method of controlling delivery of a therapeutic agent by a programmable pump, the method comprising:**

   accessing a basal delivery schedule;

   receiving a bolus request identifying a requested bolus quantity;

   allocating the requested bolus quantity among a plurality of bolus portions, including at least a first bolus portion and a second bolus portion;

   causing delivery of the first bolus portion during a first delivery interval;

   causing delivery of the second bolus portion during a second delivery interval occurring after commencement of the first delivery interval;

   receiving a temporary basal-rate instruction defining a modified basal rate and a finite duration;

   causing delivery according to the modified basal rate during the finite duration; and

   in response to termination of the finite duration, automatically causing delivery according to a then-current basal rate specified by the basal delivery schedule.

20. The method of claim 19, further comprising evaluating delivery history accumulated after delivery of the first bolus portion and adjusting the second bolus portion based on the delivery history.

21. The method of claim 19, further comprising receiving physiological measurements during a delay between the first and second bolus portions and conditionally authorizing delivery of the second bolus portion based on the physiological measurements.

22. The method of claim 19, wherein causing delivery according to the modified basal rate comprises applying a temporary multiplier to respective time-varying rates of the basal delivery schedule.

23. The method of claim 19, further comprising generating an alert before expiration of the finite duration and receiving a command to extend, cancel, or replace the temporary basal-rate instruction.

24. The method of claim 19, further comprising storing an event record identifying the requested bolus quantity, the plurality of bolus portions, the modified basal rate, the finite duration, and an automatically resumed basal rate.

---

### 25. Independent Computer-Readable Medium Claim

25. **A non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by a controller of a therapeutic-agent pump, cause the controller to:**

   control the pump according to a stored basal delivery schedule;

   divide a requested bolus quantity into at least two temporally separated bolus portions;

   control delivery of the at least two temporally separated bolus portions;

   temporarily replace or modify a basal rate of the stored basal delivery schedule for a bounded time interval; and

   automatically reinstate, upon expiration of the bounded time interval, a basal rate corresponding to a then-active portion of the stored basal delivery schedule.

26. The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 25, wherein the instructions further cause the controller to arbitrate overlapping basal and bolus deliveries according to a programmed priority rule and a cumulative delivery limit.

27. The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 25, wherein the instructions further cause the controller to discontinue a remaining bolus portion or the temporary basal-rate modification upon detection of an occlusion, depleted reservoir, low power condition, communication fault, or physiological-safety condition.

---

## Exemplary Operational Description

A user or remote control device may enter a total bolus quantity, a first-portion parameter, and a timing parameter. The first-portion parameter may define an immediately delivered quantity or percentage. The timing parameter may define a delay before a subsequent portion, a duration over which a subsequent portion is delivered, or respective delivery times for multiple subsequent portions. The controller validates the entered parameters against programmed limits and stores an executable split-bolus profile.

A temporary basal command may specify an absolute rate, a percentage of the scheduled rate, a rate differential, or a suspension rate. The command includes a finite duration or an ascertainable termination condition. While the temporary basal command remains active, the controller may track both elapsed and remaining duration. At termination, the controller identifies the basal-schedule segment applicable at that time and automatically resumes the rate associated with that segment.

Where a split bolus overlaps a temporary basal modification, the controller may maintain separate accounting records for basal and bolus quantities. The controller may interleave actuation pulses attributable to the two delivery modes, suppress basal pulses during bolus actuation, or combine commanded quantities into a composite actuation sequence, while preserving records identifying the amount attributable to each mode.
